## Verdict
REVISE — resolve controller-death recovery and stale-event ordering before enabling automatic radio changes.

## Critical gaps
- `START_STICKY` and dynamic receivers do not guarantee wake restoration after process death, force-stop, or foreground-service termination. Define fail-open recovery independent of the app, and distinguish persisted **enabled** from operational **armed**.
- A transaction lock prevents overlap, not stale decisions. Serialize reconciliation, reread current screen/power/display guards before mutation, and cancel or reverse an in-flight apply when wake/charging/display activation supersedes it.

## Important improvements
- Minimal arrangement: app foreground service owns policy decisions; root owns desired state and journal. Add one-shot boot restoration before rearming and a lifetime-bound root broker that restores on controller disconnect—not another policy loop. Promote the service before root work; register listeners before initial reconciliation; use only bounded transition wake locks.
- Archive legacy ownership markers and quiesce the verified idle-saver process before restoration. Its termination trap deletes markers even when restoration fails; the existing uninstaller also unforces Doze unconditionally.
- Preserve manual overrides for the remainder of the current screen-off episode; repeated display callbacks must not reacquire settings already relinquished.

## Validation gaps
- Device tests for API36 boot startup, process death, force-stop/foreground-service stop, APK replacement, and root denial while standby changes are applied. Verify restoration or explicit retained recovery state.
- Java controller tests for rapid screen/power/display transitions and delayed radio completion; Python helper tests alone cannot validate lifecycle ordering.
- Fault injection around every journal/write boundary, including asynchronous radio transitions, missing scan-setting values, and repeated recon...
